title: feat(tools): convert STEP bodies to DXF half-profiles and import/export DXF
body:
## What changed

- Added a clean-room ASCII DXF writer in `crates/geometry/src/dxf/writer.rs` (`dxf::write`, `dxf::write_bytes`, `Unit::code`) emitting `HEADER` (`$INSUNITS`), `TABLES` (`LAYER`), and `ENTITIES` (`LINE`, `ARC`, `CIRCLE`).
- Added conservative stepped-band reduction in `crates/tools/src/spun_envelope.rs` (`SpunProfile::conservative_from_bands`) merging adjacent `HolderBand`s strictly upward (`max(r)`) down to at most 31 bands (`<= 64` points) and `MIN_SEGMENT`.
- Added STEP and `ToolBody` <-> ASCII DXF half-profile conversion and DXF import in `crates/app/src/tool_profile_dxf.rs` and `crates/app/src/tool_profile_dxf_import.rs` with explicit `CENTRELINE` and `PROFILE` layers.
- Added undoable `SetToolBody` constructors (`from_dxf_bytes`, `from_dxf`, `from_step_profile`, `from_placed_profile`, `profile_dxf`) in `crates/app/src/commands/tool_body_dxf.rs` over `tool_body::build_spun`.
- Registered MCP tools `import_tool_holder_dxf`, `export_tool_holder_dxf`, and `convert_tool_step_to_profile` in `crates/app/src/mcp/holder_dxf_tools.rs`.
- Added conservative-envelope and half-profile-only notices, `Import DXF…`, `Export DXF…`, `Import STEP…`, and Body tab `Convert to profile` in `crates/ui/src/state_tool_profile.rs`, `tool_profile_page.rs`, and `tool_body_page.rs`.
- Recorded architectural trade-offs in `docs/decisions/743-step-dxf-half-profile.md`.

## Cause

- Direct conversion from `HolderProfile::envelope` to `SpunProfile` failed above 31 stepped bands because `2 * 32 + 2 = 66` exceeds `MAX_POINTS` (`64`).
- CamCraft lacked an ASCII DXF writer and could not export or re-import tool holder half-profiles with an explicit centreline or enforce ISO 13399 CSYS alignment on STEP-to-profile conversion.

## Tests

- Pins:
  - `camcraft-geometry::dxf_writer`: `write_and_parse_round_trip_lines_arcs_circles_layers_and_units`, `writer_refuses_invalid_inputs_by_name` (2 passed).
  - `camcraft-tools::spun::envelope::tests::thirty_two_distinct_bands_reduce_conservatively_to_spun_profile` (1 passed).
  - `camcraft-app::tool_dxf_profile` (6 passed): `step_to_dxf_half_profile_envelops_every_sampled_mesh_point`, `non_revolved_step_or_fine_32_plus_band_mesh_is_conservatively_enveloped`, `step_conversion_refuses_missing_or_ambiguous_axis_by_name`, `dxf_half_profile_import_with_lines_and_arcs_lands_as_tool_body`, `dxf_half_profile_error_refusals_never_panic_and_name_reasons`, `round_trip_step_to_dxf_to_body_to_dxf_is_stable_within_tolerance`.
  - `camcraft-app::tool_dxf_profile_mcp`: `mcp_holder_dxf_and_step_profile_tools_list_round_trip_undo_and_refuse` (1 passed).
  - `camcraft-ui::egui_app::tests::tool_profile` (9 passed, adding `profile_tab_states_conservative_envelope_and_half_profile_rules_and_dxf_workflow` and `body_tab_convert_to_profile_refuses_unaligned_step_and_converts_iso_aligned_step`).
- Mutations (each tested red after weakening the guard and green after restore):
  - `spun_envelope::join` `max(r)` -> `min(r)`: failed `thirty_two_distinct_bands_reduce_conservatively_to_spun_profile`; restored green.
  - `dxf::writer` zero-length `LINE` guard bypassed: failed `writer_refuses_invalid_inputs_by_name`; restored green.
  - `tool_profile_dxf_import` centreline-crossing guard bypassed: failed `dxf_half_profile_error_refusals_never_panic_and_name_reasons`; restored green.
  - `step_to_spun_profile` ISO 13399 requirement replaced with `+Z` fallback: failed `step_conversion_refuses_missing_or_ambiguous_axis_by_name`; restored green.
  - `convert_body_draft_to_profile` clear-axis check bypassed: failed `body_tab_convert_to_profile_refuses_unaligned_step_and_converts_iso_aligned_step`; restored green.
- Gate:
  - `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` expanded to the `batch` tier (`crates/geometry/src/dxf/mod.rs` is a shared crate) and passed all 10 steps in 39.8 min with 0 failures (`geometry`, `kernel`, `cl`, `tools`, `post`, `sim`, `motion`, `app`, `ui`, `clippy -D warnings`).

## Goldens moved

- None (`git diff --stat upstream/main -- "*.nc" "*.cl"` is empty).

## Not exercised

- Native OS file-picker modal calls (`import_profile_dxf_dialog`, `export_profile_dxf_dialog`, `import_step_profile_dialog`) delegate to desktop `rfd`; headless UI tests exercise `import_profile_dxf_from`, `export_profile_dxf_to`, `import_step_profile_from`, and `Convert to profile`.
- Release-tier `SLOW_BINARIES` (`motion:finish3d`, `motion:pivot5d`, `motion:flow`, `app:center_cut_multiaxis`) were outside the `batch` gate run.

## Overlaps

- `#2092` (stacked on `#2054`) edits different functions in `crates/app/src/commands/tool_body.rs` (`library_body`, `SetToolBody::spun`), `crates/ui/src/state_tool_profile.rs` (`sync_tool_profile_ui`, `pick_library_holder`, `run_set_tool_holder`, `editor_library_holder`), `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tool_profile_page.rs` (lines 84-87), and `crates/app/src/mcp/tools.rs` (lines 32, 38, 281); this PR uses `tool_body::build_spun` (no `ToolBody` struct literals) and companion modules/tail blocks; whichever merges second refreshes.
- `#2096` edits `envelope` and `preview_3d` in `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tool_body_page.rs`, different lines from `Convert to profile`; whichever merges second refreshes.
- `#2077` edits `crates/app/src/lib.rs` line 118 and `crates/app/src/mcp/tools.rs` line 281, different lines from our additions at `lib.rs` and the tail of `all()` in `mcp/tools.rs`; whichever merges second refreshes.


## UI screenshots

Rendered with the real egui shell harness at 1600 × 1200. Before uses the exact `upstream/main` (`a277dd9d51e7b4488403b946d0a3234b71ba7504`) Profile and Body page sources. After uses this PR's page sources. The Body tab shows the same ISO 13399 STEP fixture in both captures. Native file-picker dialogs were not exercised.

title: fix(ui): disable X/Y WCS tilt on milling setups and point to Part alignment
body:
Stacked on #1684 (merge #1684 first)

## What changed

- Added Option 1 (Slice 1) milling guard in `crates/ui/src/egui_app/wcs_page.rs`.
- On `Kind::Mill` setups (`machine::kind_of(&state.world) == Kind::Mill`), `origin_fields` disables the `Tilt about X (roll)` and `Tilt about Y (pitch)` spinbuttons and shows a hint pointing to `Part alignment` on the Setup page.
- `quarter_turns` renders the 3x2 turn buttons via `turn_row`, disabling `Turn X+`, `Turn X-`, `Turn Y+`, and `Turn Y-` on milling setups with the same hover hint.
- `X origin`, `Y origin`, `Z origin`, `Turn about Z (yaw)`, `Turn Z+`, `Turn Z-`, `Level`, and `Set Origin` stay live on milling setups.
- When an existing milling WCS is already tilted (`setup_wcs_tilt::setup_problem`), `wcs_page` warns that generation will refuse it and instructs the user to click `Level` and use `Part alignment`.
- Non-mill machines (such as `Kind::Lathe`) keep X/Y tilt spinbuttons and all six quarter-turn buttons live.
- Recorded the Option 1 choice and deferred items in `docs/decisions/1542-milling-wcs-tilt-guard.md`.

## Cause

Milling generation refuses any WCS tilted off machine Z (`setup_wcs_tilt`), while the WCS page still invited users to tilt milling WCS axes via `Tilt about X (roll)`, `Tilt about Y (pitch)`, and X/Y quarter turns instead of using `Part alignment`.

## Tests

- Pins in `crates/ui/src/egui_app/wcs_page_tests.rs`:
  - `milling_setup_disables_xy_wcs_tilt_and_points_to_part_alignment`: red before fix (`Tilt about X (roll) must be disabled on a milling setup`), green after fix.
  - `non_mill_setup_keeps_xy_wcs_tilt_and_turns_live`: verifies `Tilt about X/Y` spinbuttons and all 6 turn buttons stay live and `Turn X+` tilts the WCS on `Kind::Lathe`.
  - Updated `quarter_turns_are_equal_buttons_filling_the_pane` so `Turn Z+`/`Turn Z-` are asserted live and `Turn X±`/`Turn Y±` disabled on `with_stock()` (`Kind::Mill`), keeping equal-size and alignment assertions intact.
- Mutation checks on `crates/ui/src/egui_app/wcs_page.rs`:
  - Reverted to `base-1684`: `milling_setup_disables_xy_wcs_tilt_and_points_to_part_alignment` (`Tilt about X (roll)`) and `quarter_turns_are_equal_buttons_filling_the_pane` (`Turn X+`) both failed; green after restore.
  - Forced `turn_row` `enabled = true` and `tilted_mill = false`: both tests failed on `Turn X+`; green after restore.
  - Forced `tilted_mill = false` alone: `milling_setup_disables_xy_wcs_tilt_and_points_to_part_alignment` failed missing the tilted-WCS warning; green after restore.
- Gate and lint:
  - `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: green (`14s`, `ui suites`: `ui lib`, `ui:boundary`, `ui:boundary_picks`, `ui:sinker_setup`, `ui:theme_files`, 0 failed).
  - `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: green.

## Goldens moved

None.

## Not exercised

- Full cross-workspace gate beyond `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` (only `crates/ui` code changed).
- Feature-pick Z-tilt guard (`wcs_pick_row.rs`) and MCP `set_wcs` milling guard (Slice 2, deferred because `#1931` is relocating `wcs_pick_row.rs`; `setup_wcs_tilt` continues to block tilted milling setups at generation).

## Overlaps

- Stacked on #1684 (`quarter_turns`, `turn_wcs`, and `wcs_page_tests.rs`); merge #1684 first, then retarget or refresh this PR.
- Touches `crates/ui/src/egui_app/wcs_page.rs` alongside #1717 (`OFFSET_GROUP`, different functions/lines) and #1738 (`flip_row` inside `quarter_turns` between `Turn X-` and `Level`; this PR leaves widget placement between `Turn X-` and `Level` unchanged). Whichever merges later refreshes.

title: fix(2d): add 2D shape-mask verifier and PNG diff reporter
body:
## What changed

Added a test-only 2D toolpath shape-mask verifier under `crates/motion/tests/common/` and a pure-Rust RGB difference PNG writer with no new dependencies. The helper checks overcut, leftover, progressive rim engagement, symmetry and stock extension. Added helper regressions and generator fixtures for Adaptive and trochoidal paths. Updated the testing instructions and decision record.

Ramps contribute only their selected depth interval. Clearance records the deepest actual cutter position covering each cell. A descending helix never clears its entire footprint at its endpoint depth.

The two radial-engagement fixtures explicitly start with a predrilled 8 mm radius bore at their final floor: Adaptive at `(0, 0, -5)`, trochoidal at `(-20, 0, -6)`. The radius is the 3 mm entry orbit plus the 5 mm cutter radius. Initial stock clearance is bounded by that region and depth. It gives no swept-path coverage credit. The generated paths still must pass their original overcut, leftover, symmetry and stock-extension checks. Engagement bounds are unchanged.

## Validation

- `cargo test -p camcraft-motion --test shape_masks --test trochoid_slot --test adaptive_hsm`: 11 helper tests passed, 12 trochoidal tests passed, 2 Adaptive tests passed and 5 heavy tests stayed ignored.
- Adaptive measured maximum cut width: 1.956193 mm against a 2.352 mm limit. Trochoidal: 5.218097 mm against a 5.375 mm limit.
- Pin: `shape_mask_precleared_bore_respects_its_radius_and_depth` accepts light side cutting with the stated bore, rejects a smaller or shallower bore, rejects overload outside it, and confirms initial stock does not credit generated swept coverage. The existing solid-stock ramp and helix regressions still pass.
- Isolated mutations: disabling precleared initialization failed the new pin (2.000 mm > 0.688 mm); reverting the Adaptive fixture to solid stock failed its generator pin (10.000 mm > 2.352 mm); reverting the trochoidal fixture failed its generator pin (10.000 mm > 5.375 mm). Each restored pin passed.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: GREEN, 1,033 passed, 0 failed, 53 ignored across 86 motion test binaries (library plus 85 integration suites).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings`: GREEN.

No runtime CAM code, dependencies, goldens, screenshots or review evidence changed. Difference PNGs are temporary failure artifacts and are not committed. Heavy ignored tests and GUI suites were not run.

Process change: yes

Fixes #1768

title: feat(tools)!: a tool's library holder is a reference to the entry
body:
Stacked on #2054 (branch `mkinney:issue/2018-weldon-per-taper`, with `main` merged in for #2029). Merge #2054 first; this diff then shows only the #2016 commits. Fork synced from upstream `main` at c86d6db35.

## What changed

A tool that sits in a built-in library holder stores a reference to the entry, not a drawn copy of its outline.

- `camcraft_tools::holder_library::HolderRef {entry, gauge_len, projection}` (new, `crates/tools/src/holder_library_ref.rs`), carried on `ToolBody::library`.
- `tool_body::build_library` is the one place a reference becomes a shape. `SetToolBody::library`, `AddTool` (stated and machine-default holder), the project loader and the `.camtools` reader call it. `tool_body::judged`, `stack`, `digest`, the simulation and the preview read the body it returns, as before. The #828 floor for a machine-default holder is unchanged.
- Files: the tool key `holder: {entry, gauge_len, projection}` (plus `machine_default: true` when assumed) is written in place of `body`. Project v62 (the unreleased step the issue names); a `.camtools` file says version 2 when a tool names a library holder.
- Migration: an older file is not rewritten. A drawn copy of a library holder stays a custom drawn profile with the same outline, and a `holder_d`/`holder_len` cylinder stays the tool's own numbers.
- Refusals by tool name: an entry the library does not hold, a grouped pick ("BT40 Weldon"), lengths the entry cannot take, a holder that reaches into the flutes, an unknown key in the reference, `holder` beside `body`. No other holder is put in its place.
- MCP: `set_tool_holder` with `library` writes the reference; the reply and `get_job` show it as `holder.library`. `add_tool` refuses a `holder` reference inside `definition`; `edit_tool` refuses a `holder` patch. Skill rows updated.
- UI: with a referenced holder the tool settings show the holder diameter and length the laws read as text, not as two fields. The Profile tab names the entry and the picker shows it. The unchanged outline applied again keeps the reference; one edited point makes the holder a custom profile (one undo step).

Decisions: `docs/decisions/2016-holder-reference.md`.

## How tested

`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` green on the final head (tools, app and ui suites), and `cargo clippy -p camcraft-tools -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean. macOS (m5).

Pinning tests:

- `crates/app/tests/holder_reference.rs`
  - `every_entry_reads_the_same_bands_by_reference_as_its_old_copy`: for every library entry, at the default and at other lengths, picked and assumed: the judged tool, envelope, band stack, stamp term and facets equal those of the drawn copy an older build stored, also after a save and load.
  - `an_older_project_loads_as_custom_holders_with_the_same_collision_result`: a v61 project with a drawn copy and a plain holder cylinder loads with the same reads, operation status and warnings (the BT30 flange strikes the fixture wall, hit for hit).
  - `an_older_tool_library_loads_as_custom_holders_and_a_new_one_round_trips_the_reference`
  - `an_unknown_entry_refuses_the_file_by_name_and_never_lands_another_holder` (project and `.camtools`)
  - `a_library_holder_is_the_reference_in_the_document_and_the_file`
  - `the_unchanged_outline_keeps_the_reference_and_an_edited_point_makes_it_custom`
  - `mcp_set_tool_holder_writes_the_reference`
- `crates/tools/src/holder_library_ref.rs` unit tests.
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/tool_holder_reference.rs`: `a_library_holder_sizes_the_holder_fields_until_its_outline_is_edited`, `the_profile_tab_names_the_entry_and_the_picker_shows_it`.

## Not exercised

- Windows and Linux. The release tier and the pixel-snapshot lanes (no snapshot PNG changed).
- No real v0.21.0 file was read: the older file in the tests is this build's file rewritten to the older form (`body` with the drawn copy, version 61 / 1).
- The app was not driven by hand.

## Notes for the reviewer

- A build of main between #1453 and this change reads v62 and would drop the `holder` key (development builds only; v0.21.0 refuses v62).
- A corrected library entry now reaches every project that names it. A copy kept the old numbers.
- The tool record's `holder_d`/`holder_len` are not overwritten by the entry (they are what the tool goes back to when the holder is cleared, and writing them would move the stamp). The settings show the entry's numbers.

Changelog: A tool's library holder is stored as a reference to the library entry (name, gauge length, projection) in the project and tool library files, not as a drawn copy; the tool settings show the entry's holder size. Breaking: v0.21.0 and older refuse a file that names a library holder.

Effort: max (no escalation)

BREAKING CHANGE: a project or tool library saved with a library holder states it as a reference (project v62, `.camtools` version 2); v0.21.0 and older refuse such a file.

Process change: yes

Fixes #2016

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

https://claude.ai/code/session_01CUsqDAAAJyAPrC37zBzbbX

## UI screenshots

These images show the seeded `EM-0600-4FL` tool with the `BT30 ER20` holder.
The gauge length is 60 mm. The projection is 55 mm.

The egui test harness drives the production shell and renders these PNGs with the GPU renderer.
The before captures use the four UI and profile-state source files from `e661ece1`.
The backend stays at `822c4c9a` to supply the same holder geometry in both captures.
The after captures use the current head, `822c4c9a`.

### Holder size controls

Before: the holder diameter and length are editable fields.

![Holder size controls before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/ba10296eb7199e2b37254900e26f188302e5a1c8/2092/holder-controls-before.png)

After: the controls show the library holder diameter and length, with the entry name.

![Holder size controls after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/ba10296eb7199e2b37254900e26f188302e5a1c8/2092/holder-controls-after.png)

### Profile tab

Before: the tab identifies a drawn profile. The library picker has no selection.

![Holder Profile tab before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/ba10296eb7199e2b37254900e26f188302e5a1c8/2092/holder-profile-before.png)

After: the tab names the library holder. The picker shows `BT30 ER20`, the gauge length, and the projection.

title: fix(ui): read status strip, ribbon tabs, window margin and drop hint from theme
body:
Stacked on #2027 (merge #2027 first)

## What changed

- Added five geometry tokens to `theme::Tokens` (`window_margin`, `status_h`, `ribbon_tab_pad_x`, `ribbon_tab_gap`, `ribbon_tab_stroke`) and `clamp::RADIUS_WINDOW` (`24`).
- Updated `Tokens::DARK` and `Tokens::LIGHT` in `theme/tables.rs` with defaults that preserve existing dark and light pixel geometry (`6.0`, `22.0`, `12.0`, `2.0`, `2.0`).
- Added `theme::status_h(t)` to return the maximum of `t.status_h`, `t.control_height + 4.0`, and `t.font_row * 1.3 + 4.0`.
- Wired `Tokens::style()` to read `spacing.window_margin` from `self.window_margin` instead of `item_spacing_y.max(6.0)`.
- Wired `shell::shell_layout` to size the bottom status bar with `theme::status_h(&pal)`.
- Wired `panes::ribbon_tabs` to read left inset from `pal.item_spacing_x`, tab padding from `pal.ribbon_tab_pad_x`, inter-tab gap from `pal.ribbon_tab_gap`, and underline stroke from `pal.ribbon_tab_stroke`.
- Wired `file_drop::paint_hint` to read border inset from `pal.window_margin`, corner radius from `pal.radius_window`, and stroke thickness and text size from `pal.font_label`.
- Split `theme_files::names` into `crates/ui/src/egui_app/theme_files/names.rs` to keep every file under 400 lines.
- Added `docs/decisions/2064-theme-shell-metrics.md`.

## Cause

Shell metrics for window margin, bottom status height, ribbon tab spacing and stroke, and the file drop hint used hardcoded constants or `item_spacing_y` instead of dedicated theme tokens.

## Tests

All five pinning tests failed before the fix on unchanged `base-2027` and pass after the final edit:

- `theme_shell_metrics::window_margin_comes_from_own_token_not_item_spacing`
- `theme_shell_metrics::status_h_and_ribbon_tab_keys_parse_and_clamp`
- `egui_app::tests::ribbon_rows::issue_2064_pins::status_strip_height_tracks_theme_controls_and_status_h`
- `egui_app::tests::ribbon_rows::issue_2064_pins::ribbon_tabs_follow_theme_spacing_pad_gap_and_stroke`
- `egui_app::tests::file_drop::issue_2064_pins::drop_hint_reads_window_margin_radius_and_font_from_theme`

Mutation checks (each reverted or loosened code path failed red, then passed green after restoring):

1. `theme.rs` `Tokens::style()` `window_margin` reverted to `item_spacing_y.max(6.0)` -> `window_margin_comes_from_own_token_not_item_spacing` failed, restored passed.
2. `theme_files/overlay.rs` clamps on the 5 new keys loosened -> `status_h_and_ribbon_tab_keys_parse_and_clamp` failed, restored passed.
3. `theme.rs` `status_h()` stripped to `t.status_h` -> `status_strip_height_tracks_theme_controls_and_status_h` failed, restored passed.
4. `shell.rs` `.exact_size(22.0)`, `panes.rs` `ribbon_tabs` literals, and `file_drop.rs` `paint_hint` literals reverted -> all 3 `issue_2064_pins` tests failed, restored passed.

Gate and lint after final edit:

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: passed (`ui lib` 832 passed / 6 ignored, `boundary` 3, `boundary_picks` 6, `sinker_setup` 2, `theme_files` 14, `theme_shell_metrics` 2, `waterjet_tool` 1; 0 failed).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: passed with zero warnings.

## Goldens moved

None (`0` `.nc`, `.cl`, or `.png` files changed).

## Not exercised

- `assets/themes/theme.json.example` was not updated here because #2038 creates that file on top of #2027 and this branch stacks one level on #2027.
- Unchanged non-UI workspace crates and Windows-made pixel snapshot goldens did not run in the quick gate.

## Overlaps

- `#2027` (stacked on it; merge `#2027` first): modifies `theme.rs` (`Tokens`, `clamp`, `geom_legal`), `theme/tables.rs`, `theme_files.rs` (`names`, `COLOR_NAMES`, `GEOM_NAMES`), `theme_files/overlay.rs` (`apply_overlay`), `shell.rs` (constants above `STATUS_H`), `panes.rs` (`ribbon_tabs`), and `tests/ribbon_rows.rs`.
- `#2029`, `#2023`, `#1798`, `#1330` touch other functions in `shell.rs`; `#1798` touches other functions in `panes.rs`. Whichever merges second refreshes.

Changelog: Read status strip height, ribbon tab metrics, window margin, and drop hint geometry from theme tokens
Fixes #2064

## Review screenshots

These screenshots show the actual shell, tool editor, and file drop hint.
The renderer uses `egui_kittest` and the actual `View3D` GPU output at 1440 × 960 pixels.
The ribbon and status images are crops of that output.

Both runs use the same dark theme and scene.
The theme sets `window_margin=20`, `status_h=48`, `ribbon_tab_pad_x=24`, `ribbon_tab_gap=12`, and `ribbon_tab_stroke=6`.
It also sets `item_spacing_x=16`, `radius_window=20`, and `font_label=15`.
These values make the changed behavior visible. The default values preserve the previous geometry.

The after run uses the consumers at `bacb784b0207c43ea610bb8da9c8beb15f9ba61b`.
For the before run, the temporary harness restores the parent ribbon tab function, status height, window margin expression, and drop hint body.
The before run keeps the new token schema to load the same theme file.
It keeps an unused palette argument on the drop hint function so the harness compiles.
Thus, the before run shows the parent consumer behavior with the same theme configuration.
It does not use an unchanged parent checkout.

The eight PNG files exist only on the fork's `pr-screenshots` branch.
No screenshot, capture harness, log, or review evidence was added to this PR branch.

title: fix(ui): --help lists every start option and variable
body:
## What changed

- New table `crates/ui/src/cli_options.rs`. It lists each start option and each environment variable. The option check and the `--help` text read this one table.
- `--help`, `-h` and `--version` print and exit with code 0. This happens before any window or GPU device is made.
- An unknown option exits with code 2. The message names the option and points to `--help`.
- New user guide page `docs/user-guide/start-options.md`.
- Decision file: `docs/decisions/2082-help-options.md`.

## Printed `--help` text

```
camcraft-ui - a CAM program that turns 3D models into NC programs

Usage: camcraft-ui [options]

Options:
  -h, --help
      Print this text and exit. No window opens.
      Default: off
  --version
      Print the program version and exit. No window opens.
      Default: off
  --headless
      Start with no window. Run a short self-check of the 3D view and exit.
      Default: off
  --ui <name>
      Choose the user interface. Only "egui" exists.
      Default: egui
  --gpu-backend <dx12|metal|vulkan|gl>
      Try this graphics system first. The other systems stay as a fallback.

      Default: automatic
  --gpu <adapter name>

      Default: automatic
  --mcp-port <port>
      Open the MCP server for AI agents on this local port (0 to 65535).
      Environment variable: CAMCRAFT_MCP_PORT. The option wins over the variable.

  CAMCRAFT_GPU_BACKEND <dx12|metal|vulkan|gl>
```

title: feat(tools)!: cutting data by work material - Unknown default row, stepdown/stepover, stock material
body:
## What changed

Tool cutting data by work material (#2015, part of #2007):

- **`Unknown` row.** Every tool's cutting data now holds an `Unknown` row (file word `unknown`; in code `CuttingRow::material == None`). It is what the tool runs when no row names the material in force, and the fallback for a row's missing stepdown/stepover. It is derived from the tool's own rpm/feed and stored only when it states something more (other numbers, or a step) - so a new tool has it, every older tool reads its own numbers as it, and plain tools are stored, saved and shown to MCP byte for byte as before. A command that moves the running numbers away from a derived row stores it first. A waterjet (recipes) and an electrode (rpm 0) get none, so a sane tool never turns insane.
- **Stepdown and stepover per row** (mm, optional). They seed an operation's stepdown/stepover only inside an undoable command (quick-add, MCP `add_operation`, the feature recognizer, `SetWorkMaterial`, `SetStockMaterial`, retargeting a tool), never on load. Seeded kinds: pocket, adaptive, offset, slot, 3-D pocket, multi-axis rough, face (stepover; stepdown only when staged), 2-D contour (stepdown). A stepover wider than the cutter is refused by tool name.
- **Setup stock material.** New `StockMaterial` component on a setup's stock and the undoable `SetStockMaterial` command (MCP `set_stock_material`, stock page "Material" group). The row is picked by the stock's material, then the document's, then `Unknown`. The tools' running rpm/feed (the posted S word) follow the document material only - a tool is shared by every setup.
- **`.camtools`/project migration.** `PROJECT_VERSION` 62 -> 63 (the issue's "61 to 62" predates #1453's bump). A v62 project loads with each tool's own rpm/feed as its `Unknown` row; nothing it runs moves. `.camtools` reader accepts versions 1, 2 and 3; the writer writes 3 only when a library holds a stated `Unknown` row or a step (otherwise 1, or 2 for left-hand taps, as before). An `Unknown` row that only repeats the tool's own rpm/feed is not written, so plain tools save byte for byte as before (MCP `get_job` output unchanged for them).
- **Tool page.** The "Cutting data by material" group is now a table: Material, Spindle rpm, Feed, Stepdown, Stepover (0 = not stated). The `Unknown` row is first, its material fixed, not removable.
- **Behaviour change, inside a command only:** stating a document material the tool has no row for now runs the tool's `Unknown` row (before: the previous material's numbers stayed). An operation's milling feed still moves only for a row that names the material (#890's rule), so picking a material never overwrites hand-set op feeds.

Decisions: `docs/decisions/2015-unknown-cutting-row.md` (why `Option<WorkMaterial>` and not a `WorkMaterial::Unknown` variant: `WorkMaterial::row()` indexes the handbook table).

Base: upstream/main (`31f8d03d7`); no file overlap with #2029 (it does not touch `tool_cutting_rows.rs`; both touch `crates/ui/src/state.rs` in different places). Fork synced at the current upstream main for this branch.

## How tested

Pinning tests:
- `crates/tools/tests/unknown_row.rs` (6): selection order, step fallback, derivation once and only from the running numbers, kinds that get none, refusals (bad steps, `Unknown` twice).
- `crates/app/tests/cutting_unknown_row.rs` (9): `a_new_tool_gets_its_unknown_row_from_its_own_numbers`, `a_v62_project_loads_its_tool_numbers_as_the_unknown_row_with_no_loss`, `a_v1_tool_library_loads_with_the_unknown_row_and_steps_write_v3`, `the_row_is_picked_by_the_stock_then_the_document_then_unknown`, `a_second_setup_stock_material_seeds_only_its_own_operations`, `steps_seed_only_in_commands_and_the_stock_material_round_trips`, `a_project_with_no_new_rows_posts_the_same_s_and_f_words` (posts, re-saves as v62, reloads, re-posts: identical S/F words), `a_stated_stepover_wider_than_the_cutter_is_refused_by_tool_name`, `mcp_sets_the_stock_material_as_one_undo_step`.
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/stock_material.rs`: the stock page's Material group sits between Shape and Size, and a pick is one undoable `SetStockMaterial`.
- Updated to the new law: `crates/app/tests/tool_cutting_rows.rs` (stating plastics, which has no row, now runs the tool's Unknown row), `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tool_cutting_rows.rs` unit tests (Unknown is shown, never added).

Gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` (macOS, m5): green on 75031d5f9 (tools, app and ui suites; 6.2 min). Clippy on camcraft-tools, camcraft-app, camcraft-ui: clean (`--all-targets -D warnings`).

## Not exercised

- No hands-on UI run of the new table or the stock Material picker (unit/structural suites only); the pixel snapshots were not run (release lane) and no PNG changed.
- The camcraft-mcp skill row for `set_stock_material` is a follow-up (process-file change): #2076.
- A per-setup spindle speed (the S word by stock material) is out of scope: the tool's running rpm follows the document material.

Changelog: Tools keep cutting data per work material with an Unknown default row, an optional stepdown and stepover per row, and a setup stock may state its own material, which picks the row (stock, then document, then Unknown); older projects and tool libraries load unchanged (#2015)

Effort: high (no escalation)

BREAKING CHANGE: project files are written as version 63 (and tool libraries with a stated Unknown row or steps as version 3); older builds refuse them.

Fixes #2015

title: fix(xtask): share one job budget across the lanes of a gate wave
body:
## What changed

- New `xtask/src/budget.rs`: one job budget for each gate run. The default is 6 (`budget::DEFAULT`). `CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=<n>` (1 or more) overrides it. A bad value prints a note and keeps 6.
- `exec.rs` sets `-j` and `--test-threads=` of each step when it runs the step (`budget::scale`):
  - A wave of N lanes gives each lane `budget / N` jobs, minimum 1.
  - A step that runs alone gets the full budget. This applies to each quick, batch and test step, and to each release step that runs alone.
  - A value that a step sets on purpose (not the plan default `6`) can only go down.
- `lanes::waves(steps, limit)` takes the lane limit. The release tier gives `budget::lane_limit` = `budget / 2`, minimum 1. `LIMIT = 4` is removed. A budget of 6 gives 3 lanes of 2 jobs.
- The gate prints the budget line at the start, and `-- wave K: N lane(s) x -j M` before each wave. `--dry-run` prints the same lines.
- The `gate` and `runners` skills have the rule: the sum of `-j` of all builds on one machine stays at or below its core count.
- `docs/decisions/2057-gate-job-budget.md` records the choices.

## Overlap with #1952 (#1941)

The plan builders (`plan.rs`, `quick.rs`, `single.rs`) do not change. The executor rewrites the flags at run time. Thus each step that #1952 adds also gets the budget. `git merge-tree` of this branch with the head of #1952 is clean, so this PR does not stack on it. After the two PRs merge, one line of `docs/decisions/1941-gate-step-per-binary.md` ("four at most") is old. The cut can correct it when it collects the decisions.

## Readings

`cargo xtask gate release --dry-run` (start):

```
gate budget: 6 job(s) (CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS overrides); at most 3 lane(s) per wave; 1 lane(s) x -j 6, 2 lane(s) x -j 3, 3 lane(s) x -j 2
-- wave 1: 1 lane(s) x -j 6
[01] debug build (--no-run)
...
-- wave 3: 3 lane(s) x -j 2
[03] geometry suites
     (cwd issue-2057) cargo test -j 2 -p camcraft-geometry --no-fail-fast -- --test-threads=2
```

`CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=4 cargo xtask gate batch --dry-run` prints `gate budget: 4 job(s); steps run one at a time with -j 4` and `-j 4 ... --test-threads=4` on each step.

## Pinning tests (`xtask/src/budget_tests.rs`)

- `wave_jobs_sum_to_at_most_the_budget_and_lanes_to_at_most_half` (budgets 1 to 16)
- `budget_six_gives_three_lanes_of_two_jobs`
- `a_step_alone_keeps_the_full_budget`
- `scale_keeps_deliberate_values_low_and_child_args_alone`
- `the_override_must_be_a_whole_number_of_one_or_more`

The `lanes_tests.rs` tests now give the limit 4 explicitly. The executor test sets the budget to 6, so that its two lanes overlap with each value of `CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS`.

Gate: `cargo test -j 2 -p xtask -- --test-threads=2` (143 + 3 + 3 passed), `cargo clippy -j 2 -p xtask --all-targets -- -D warnings` (clean), `cargo xtask gate release --dry-run`.

## Not exercised

- No real batch or release gate ran. A post-merge gate was in progress and the machine had a high load.
- The wall times of one batch run and one release wave, before and after, were not measured. The "Done means" item for them is still open; the next release gate or post-merge run gives the "after" value.
- The budget does not see other builds on the machine (reviews, workers). The skills give that rule to each build.

Process change: yes

Changelog: none

Effort: high (no escalation)

Fixes #2057

title: fix(post): honor or refuse G83 dwell per control
body:
Stacked on #1821 (merge #1821 first)

## What changed

Fanuc, Doosan DNM and Mazak refuse a positive G83 dwell by name.
Zero-dwell G83 remains available.
Haas keeps integer milliseconds and includes dwell in its G83 cycle signature.
Haas writes P0 to clear a previous dwell.

## Cause

The posts wrote P without checking G83 support for each control.
Haas omitted dwell from its cycle signature and omitted zero P.
That could reuse an earlier dwell.
Fanuc's standard milling G83 format has no P.
Mazak's detailed format and summary disagree, so this post refuses dwell conservatively.
The decision record links the public control manuals and explains these limits.

## Tests

Seven pins pass in camcraft-post's g83_dwell suite:

- fanuc_refuses_g83_dwell
- mazak_refuses_g83_dwell
- doosan_refuses_g83_dwell
- g83_without_dwell_remains_available
- haas_g83_writes_integer_milliseconds
- haas_g83_updates_dwell_in_an_open_cycle_group
- haas_g83_zero_dwell_clears_modal_p

Six pins failed on unchanged posts.
The existing Haas milliseconds behavior passed before the fix.
Replacing each of the four posts with upstream/main code made its affected pins fail.
Restoring each fix made them pass.
Removing the Haas signature change and the P0 change separately also failed their pins.
Restoring each change passed.

cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main passed with zero failures.
The final run took 18.2 minutes and included the expanded app integration selection.
cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings passed separately for camcraft-post and camcraft-app.
The initial gate hit a sandbox denial in the optional sccache preprocessor directory.
Command-line Cargo configuration disabled that cache and cleared RUSTC_WRAPPER for the successful gate.
Repository configuration did not change.

## Goldens moved

crates/app/tests/golden/nc/synth_haas.nc adds P0 to its single G83 line.
No other golden change belongs to this issue.
The two-dot comparison against current upstream lists 139 golden files because the parent is older.
Each was checked against base-1821.
The inherited differences comprise decimal formatting, G76 fixtures, and the six parent bore fixtures.
Only the synth_haas P0 word differs from the parent in this patch.

## Not exercised

No real CNC control or GUI was exercised.
Doosan OEM MV0009OPE241_v0 behavior was not publicly verified.
Mazak G83 dwell support remains ambiguous in the cited manual.
Optional Fanuc small-hole mode is not selected by these posts.
Batch and release gates were not run.

## Overlaps

PR #1821 changes onCycle in the same four posts.
This branch starts at its head, 1c06a3e1.
PR #1738 touches the same file, different function; whichever merges second refreshes.
Its overlaps are formatting, block, toolNote, onParameter, afterOp and onProbeResult.
Neither the new test nor the changed golden overlaps an open PR.

title: fix(2d): clear Zigzag rest boundaries without wall cusps
body:
Stacked on #1817 (merge #1817 first)

## What changed

2D rest machining now accepts Zigzag. It cuts rows, then closes each rest boundary to clear wall cusps.

Rows use an inset of `min(0.01 mm, stepover / 4)`. This prevents numeric boundary crossings without removing interior rows from small pockets.

The existing plain-pocket row algorithm moves unchanged to `pocket_zigzag.rs`. `pocket.rs` stays at 398 lines. No dependency is added.

The MCP skill now describes Zigzag support. Adaptive still has its named refusal. The entered previous tool remains an explicit trust assumption.

The remaining #1490 work has separate issues: Adaptive #2031, entry from cleared space #2032, and previous-operation stock #2033.

## Cause

Rows alone leave cusps at the rest boundary. A closing pass clears them. Rows that touch the boundary can cross it through numeric rounding.

A fixed 0.01 mm inset removes all rows from a tiny pocket. The stepover cap preserves those rows.

The geometry follows this project's existing scan and offset routines. See Held's [Zigzag Pocket Machining](https://www.cosy.sbg.ac.at/~held/projects/pocket_zig/pocket.html) and [pocket geometry monograph](https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/3-540-54103-9). [Yao, Gupta and Nau](https://www.cs.umd.edu/~nau/papers/yao2003algorithms.pdf) provide the cutter-coverage context. The inset and closing-pass choices are ours.

## Tests

- `zigzag_rest_covers_corner_residue_without_gouges_or_unsafe_rapids`: red at the original refusal. Green after the fix. Covers both directions and 1.5/4 mm steps.
- `tiny_rest_pocket_keeps_interior_rows_when_previous_tool_fits_nowhere`: red with the fixed inset. Green with the stepover cap.
- Expected-change tests now accept Zigzag at the motion and operation parameter doors.
- Closing-pass mutation: red coverage; restored green. The first fixture left 287 measured residue points uncut.
- Zero-inset mutation: red verifier, with six crossings; restored green.
- Fixed-inset mutation: red tiny-pocket center coverage; restored green.
- Old `upstream/main` pocket code: red; restored green.
- Old `base-1817` rest strategy: red refusal; restored green. The parent baseline supplies the export absent from `upstream/main`.

The requested `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` passed all three steps in 34.4 minutes before the inset cap.

After the cap, `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main --only motion` passed its affected motion step in 663 seconds.

`cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` passed on the final code.

## Goldens moved

None from #1490. The diff against `base-1817` changes no `.nc` or `.cl` file.

The two-dot diff against `upstream/main` lists 147 files. All were checked against the merge base and parent.
Of these, 146 exactly reverse upstream changes absent from the older parent branch. The other is #1817's unchanged `pocket_rest_corners.cl` addition.

## Not exercised

No real machine was used. This change does not implement new Adaptive paths, cleared-space entry, or previous-operation stock input.
Those features require separate depth and cutter-clearance proofs in #2031, #2032, and #2033.

## Overlaps

- #1817 changes `rest_pocket`, `rest_strategy`, and the expected-refusal tests. This branch stacks on its head.
- #2013 and #1954 touch the same file, different module declarations in `machining2d/mod.rs`; whichever merges second refreshes.
- #1738 touches the same file, a different section of the MCP skill; whichever merges second refreshes.

Decision record: `docs/decisions/1490-rest-strategies.md`.

Changelog: 2D rest Zigzag clears wall cusps with closing passes and preserves interior rows in small pockets.

Process change: yes

Effort: max

Fixes #1490

title: feat(motion): cut the adaptive stock ring from the air (issue 1950, rounds A-B)
body:
﻿Draft. Rounds A to E of issue #1950 (a default whole-model Adaptive 3D Pocket exceeds the planner budgets on the stock ring). This PR does not close the issue: the D plate level still goes to the Offset rings, now by the hop budget. Round F is open.

Head: c3509172c331eedacbf61f8a07855cadd12fdb75

## What changed

Round A (motion crate):
- New planner `plan_from_air` in `crates/motion/src/machining2d/adaptive/air_rings.rs`. It cuts the stock ring from the air side inward. Sources: Held 1991 (LNCS 500), Held and Spielberger 2009 (CAD 41(7)), Stori and Wright 2000.
- `Raster::open_air` marks the air band as open. The walk functions of `raster.rs` moved to `raster/walk.rs` with no change of logic.

Round B (plumbing, no new algorithm):
- `machining3d::open_sides` takes a `stock_band` argument. `machining3d::stock_band(r, adaptive)` gives `2r + OPEN_SLACK` for Adaptive and `r - OPEN_SLACK` for each other strategy.
- New entry `machining3d::pocket3d_open_prev(facets, footprint, stock, p, mask)`. The stock goes through `ladder`, `hsm::plan_level`, `adaptive_passes` and `hsm_passes`.
- A plan from the air whose worst reading is over the load bound is refused by name. The level then goes to the Offset rings with a note.

Round C:
- App arm (`crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs`, `open_side.rs`): a whole-model 3D Pocket with the Adaptive strategy (not shell, not rest roughing) uses the wide band and calls `pocket3d_open_prev` with the setup stock outline. Multi-Axis Rough, shell, rest roughing and each other strategy keep the old band.
- Microlift joins (`adaptive/air_links.rs`): each pass is joined to the one before it by the existing `LinkLaw`. Each join is walked again on the stock. A pass with no proved join keeps its retract hop. Source: Otkur and Lazoglu 2007.

Round D:
- Air entry: `machining2d::in_air(stock, e, r)`. Where the first pass of an air plan starts 0.005 mm clear of the stock outline, the ladder enters the level by an axial plunge there. A tool that is not centre-cutting keeps the old entry law.
- Fixture refusal: `air_band_refusal` refuses the Adaptive whole-model op at generation when a tagged fixture meets the air band. The message starts with `AIR_BAND_FIXTURE` and names the fixture. The post gate is not changed.

Round E:
- Cause of the round D crossing at (-8.12, -35.61). A probe printed the crossing pairs of the air passes before and after the joins. Before the joins: 40 pairs. After the joins: the same 40 pairs. So the joins and the air entry did not cause it. Pass 0 is the spiral (3 closed fronts and a closing lap on ring 3 at y -35.607). Passes 1-21 are open-front runs. Passes 22-45 are wall laps. The pairs were:
  - the spiral and the first open runs: a lead-in starts one load width back, on the ring 3 lap, and steps past it;
  - each open run and the run of the next front (1-4, 4-7, ...);
  - open runs and wall laps (4-37, 7-22, ...): a run that meets the part wall cuts across the laps.
- Fix, `crates/motion/src/machining2d/adaptive/air_uncross.rs` (new): each new pass drops the chords that cross a kept pass, by the plan's own law (`guard::crosses`). The pass then continues as a new piece. Each piece is read on the stock as before, so the rest and the load readings stay true. Result: 0 crossing pairs before the joins.
- The joins: with the bare passes clean, `LinkLaw::late` (a lead whose graze joins the pass) put crossings back, because the lead runs back across an earlier pass. `air_joins` now keeps a late join only when the grown pass crosses no other pass. If it crosses, the join falls back to the retract hop. Result: 0 crossing pairs after the joins.
- The crossing check, the load check, the verify gate and the budgets are not changed.
- `crates/motion/src/machining3d/descent.rs` (427 lines) is split. The landing spots (wall margin, spots along the first pass, the helix placement, the plunge spot) move to `machining3d/descent_place.rs` (120 lines) with no change of logic. `descent.rs` is now 327 lines.

## Readings, round E (D plate, R = 5, 70 x 70 stock, one level, debug)

| Reading | Round C/D (crossing plan) | Round E |
|---|---|---|
| Crossing through `adaptive_passes` | at (-8.12, -35.61) | none |
| Passes | 47 | 61 |
| Retract hops (budget 8) | 3 | 23 |
| Worst load (of D) | 0.153760 at (29.77, 22.31) | 0.153760 at (29.77, 22.31) |
| Slack to the bound | 0.00135 deg | 0.00135 deg |
| Moves (budget 120000) | 17614 | 17549 |
| Cut / air / lift (mm) | - / - / 107.3 | 2632 / 338 / 108 |
| Rest (limit 0.02) | 0.0000 | 0.0000 |
| Time, one level (debug) | 21.8 s | 22.0 s |
| Strategy of the level | Offset rings (crossing) | Offset rings (hop budget) |

22 of the 23 hops are late joins that were refused because their lead crosses an earlier pass. The earlier reading of 3 hops came from joins whose leads crossed. The hop budget was not raised.

## Posted G-code

- Changed. Each whole-model 3D Pocket with the Adaptive strategy and a stock outline uses the wide band. A level whose air plan is clean and in its budgets is cut from the air. Other levels go to the Offset rings by name, as before.
- On the D plate, the stock ring level is still cut by the Offset rings (by name, now for the hop budget).
- Multi-Axis Rough, shell, rest roughing and the non-Adaptive strategies post as before.

## Pinning tests

- `machining2d::adaptive::air_uncross::tests::a_crossing_chord_is_dropped_and_the_pass_goes_on` (new).
- `machining2d::pocket_hsm::ring_tests::the_stock_ring_level_plans_adaptive_with_no_budget_note`: still red, now on the hop budget (23 over 8). Ignored with a round F reason.
- `machining2d::pocket_hsm::ring_tests::the_stock_ring_level_reaches_the_air_planner_with_the_stock`: red on its hop assert (23 over 8). Ignored with a round F reason. Its rest and move asserts hold.
- `no_stock_keeps_the_growth_spiral`, `an_air_plan_over_the_load_bound_is_refused_by_name`: pass.
- `pocket3d_air_band`: 4 pass.

Round E runs:
- `cargo test -p camcraft-motion --lib -- ring_tests air_rings air_uncross machining3d pocket adaptive`: 87 pass, 0 fail, 9 ignored (built before the descent split; the split is a move only, and clippy built it clean).
- App: `level_links` 25, `open_band` 7, `operations` 120 / 6 ignored, `pocket3d_air_band` 4, `pocket3d_hsm` 1 / 2 ignored, `pocket3d_open_side` 7, `whole_model_pocket` 5 / 1 ignored. All pass (after the split).

title: fix(ui): lay a lathe's spindle axis across the viewport
body:
## What changed

The cause of #1993 is in the camera, not in the envelope. The envelope already is a cylinder about world Z for a lathe (`crates/post/src/machine/envelope.rs:27-60`). The turning paths also use world Z as the spindle axis. But `Camera::basis_right` (`crates/ui/src/viewport.rs`, before this PR: `normalize([fy, -fx, 0.0])`) always crossed the view with world +Z. Thus world Z could never lie across the screen, and each cylinder about Z stood vertical.

- New `crates/ui/src/view_frame.rs`: `ViewFrame { Mill, Lathe }`, a proper rotation between the orbit frame and the world. `Mill` is the identity. `Lathe`: local x = world -Z, local y = world +Y, local z = world +X.
- `Camera` gets a `frame` field. `eye` and `basis_right` map through the frame. `basis_up`, `mvp`, `ray_through`, `dolly_cursor`, the traced-stock eye and the view cube read that one basis. Draw and pick stay on one matrix.
- `Camera::toward` converts the world direction of the view cube into the frame. `Camera::pan` now uses the Z part of the right vector (it was always zero before).
- `Camera::with_frame` sets a frame and its home view. `view_frame::sync` runs at the top of `viewport_panel` in each frame. It reads `camcraft_app::machine::kind_of` (the machine of the active setup). A change of frame takes the home view of the frame. Fit and "nothing to frame" keep the frame.
- Screen rule for a lathe: the right-handed program frame (ISO 841) does not change. The home view puts world +Z (the spindle axis, away from the chuck) to the right and world +X (the cross-slide) up. World +Y then points to the viewer. The frame comes from the machine kind in the machine data, not from a hard-coded hand per machine.

Display only. The world, the WCS, the toolpaths and the posted G-code do not change: no post or generator code reads `Camera`. The frame change is view state, not a command (the test checks that the history does not change).

The decision record is `docs/decisions/1993-lathe-envelope-axis.md`.

## What #2019 still needs

This PR does the camera part. #2019 stays open for:

- The world gizmo: show Z and X only on a lathe, and Y only when the machine has a Y axis.
- A decision for mill-turn machines (this PR keeps them in the milling frame).
- View cube face names for the lathe frame, if the maintainer wants them (the cube now names world directions in each frame).
- The pin that the posted program of a turning golden does not change.

## Overlap

PR #2006 changes `crates/ui/src/work_envelope.rs`. This PR does not touch that file. PR #1689 changes `Camera::eye` and `Camera::mvp` in `crates/ui/src/viewport.rs`. This PR changes `Camera::eye` too, so a small merge conflict can occur in `eye`.

## Refresh (merge of main 17a8c6e76)

- New head: 4eb577be305761c352696384cf4426ae8f207de4 (old head c620c1255b710ce1bce0e368c542c94db255f901).
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests.rs`: both sides added a test module after `mod work_envelope;`. The merge keeps the two: `mod lathe_view;` (#1993) and `mod camera_target;` (#1997).
- `crates/ui/src/state.rs` merged without a conflict. `reset_for_open` now calls `frame_all` (#1997). `frame_all` keeps the camera frame (this PR), and `view_frame::sync` keeps the target and the distance. Thus an open frames the part, and a lathe keeps its frame.
- Tests after the merge (debug, `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib`, filters lathe_view, camera_target, view_frame, work_envelope, camera, frame, viewcube, orbit, pan): 63 passed, 0 failed, 1 ignored. This includes `lathe_view::*` (3 tests), `camera_target::frame_target_is_the_same_with_the_envelope_on_and_off` and `camera_target::open_frames_the_part_with_the_envelope_on_and_off`.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Delta class: DELTA (one hand-resolved file, `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests.rs`).

## Tests

Pinned by these tests in `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/lathe_view.rs`:

- `a_lathe_lays_the_envelope_along_the_spindle_axis_left_to_right`: through the real shell, a lathe machine file gives the lathe frame and its home view. Screen right is world +Z and screen up is world +X. The envelope ends stay at the Z travel (-197, 3). The projected spindle axis is level, +Z is to the right, and the X radius goes up. The history does not change.
- `a_mill_again_takes_the_milling_view_back`: a mill machine file again gives the milling frame and the house isometric.
- `the_lathe_frame_keeps_pick_pan_and_the_view_cube_on_one_basis`: in the lathe frame, the basis is orthonormal and right-handed, the centre ray hits the target, a pan moves along the spindle axis, and the view cube and orbit keep the frame.

Existing tests run (debug, `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib`, filters law_tests, viewcube, eye_geom, view_names, orbit, pan, iso, box_select, one_pick_rule, wcs_circle, wcs_part_point, wcs_pick_click, work_envelope, frame, edge_click, review_1710, camera, lathe_view): 144 passed, 0 failed. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Not exercised

- No visible app window was opened. The screenshots below come from an offscreen render.
- The pixel snapshots (release lane) are not run. The lathe view does not change a mill snapshot.

Changelog: The viewport shows a lathe with its spindle axis from left to right and the cross-slide up, so the work envelope lies along the spindle axis (#1993).

Effort: high (no escalation)

Fixes #1993

## Screenshots

Method: the real shell and the viewport, rendered offscreen at 1280x800 by the UI test harness. No app window was opened. The same steps run before and after: mount a lathe machine with Z travel -197 to 3, turn on "Show work envelope", then set the camera target to (0, 0, -97) and the distance to 420.

Before (origin/main, 2f6de7c5b). The envelope cylinder stands upright:

![before: lathe envelope](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/1f3a51015cc13780c217388ed587a932e61ee5ea/pr-2023/lathe-before.png)

After (this PR, c620c1255). The spindle axis runs left to right. The cylinder lies along it:

![after: lathe envelope](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/1f3a51015cc13780c217388ed587a932e61ee5ea/pr-2023/lathe-after.png)

body:
**Round 6 done (head `185a69f1e06bd7737a3c35c2ed1ae74c6716c112`). The goldens are regenerated and read. The full quick gate is not run (its plan is all app suites). The PR stays a draft.**

## Round 6 (head `185a69f1e06bd7737a3c35c2ed1ae74c6716c112`)

Merged `origin/main` (29 commits, no conflict). `emit_level` moved to `crates/motion/src/machining2d/trochoid_level.rs` (plain move, 400-line law). The CRLF files of earlier rounds are LF again.

Goldens regenerated with `WRITE_GOLDEN=1` and read. In each file the only change is the loss of the level at Top Z (it cut air) and its links. No gouge, verify, load, collision or solid check is loosened.

| Golden | Moves or lines | Read diff |
|---|---|---|
| `golden_cl` 11 files (slot, trace, contour, pocket, face stepped) | for example `contour_disc_hole` 69 to 46, `face_square_40x40_stepped` 48 to 36 | one contiguous deletion of the Z 0 level (Z 2 for the stepped face) |

| `contour_bore_arc_entry.cl` | 27 to 18 | the Z 0 level is gone. The first entry arc is on the same radius 6 circle and starts at the plunge height Z 2 |
| `contour_start_point.cl` | 43 to 29 | the Z 0 level is gone |
| `contour_control_comp.nc`, `contour_wear_comp.nc` (fanuc, haas, mazak, sinumerik) | 11 to 16 lines fewer | the Z 5 level is gone. The wear comment moves to the first comp pass |
| `fanuc-lathe/facing.nc`, `facing_css.nc`, `inch/fanuc-lathe/facing.nc` | 5 lines fewer | the rung at the work top (Z 16) is gone. The first pass is Z 15.5 |

| post inputs `vertical_arc_{x,y,oblique}.cl` (round 5) | 33 to 22, 54 to 40 | the Z 0 level is gone |

Fixtures:
- `golden_cl::face_square_40x40_stepped`: plunges 4 to 3 (levels 0.5, -1.0, -2.0).
- `solid_law_goldens::a_lead_on_the_rings_own_circle_is_refused`: the crossings of the lost level go (Arc 4, Tangential 8). Each one still refuses.
- `thread_boss::a_part_wall_the_roughing_left_standing_in_the_sweep_is_refused`: the rib top is 12 (it was 16). With levels `[15, 10]`, a rib top over 15 makes the roughing refuse its first level by name ("every contour ring cuts into the part at its first level"). The old roughing walked only the air level 20. At 12 the roughing walks 15, stops above the rib, and the thread air law still refuses "stands at z 12.000".

Readings (debug), round 6, each green:
- app: `golden_cl` 33, `conformance` 7, `solid_law_goldens` 7, `program_units` 7, `arc_entry` 3, `contour_start_point` 8, `control_comp` 5, `wear_comp` 5, `lathe_post` 7, `lathe_post_css` 10, `lathe_post_inch` 6, `adaptive_trochoid` 12, `microarc_test_part` 2, `thread_boss` 12, `engrave_law` 9, `mill2d_b` 9, `verify` 21, `trochoid_confine` 6, `trochoid_law` 7, `trochoid_op` 5, `top_z_stock_over` 2, `tinyg_post` 18, `tormach_post` 10, `tormach_end_units` 7, `program_comments` 4, `post_cycle_feed_spindle` 8, `plasma_post_refusals` 7, and the lathe, wire, sinker, c-axis and probe post suites; lib `ladder_planes`.
- motion: `top_z_level` 13, `machining2d` 66, `vertical_arc_entry` 3, `trochoid_slot` 11. post: `vertical_arc_entry` 3, `arc_planes` 7, `fanuc_post` 12.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

Not exercised: the full quick gate (all app suites), the heavy and `--ignored` lanes, a run on a real control, and operations that have no golden.

Changelog: Depth-stepping operations no longer cut a first level at Top Z when no stock stands over Top Z; posted programs have one level fewer.

Effort: high (no escalation).


## What changed

- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/levels.rs`: the shared level law `cut_levels` starts at `top - stepdown` and ends at `bottom` exactly. `top 20, bottom 0, step 5` gives `[15, 10, 5, 0]`. Each level below the first is the same float as before. `cut_levels` is now `pub`.
- Round 3: `cut_levels_under(top, material_top, bottom, stepdown)`. When the material top stands over Top Z, the level at Top Z stays (the old ladder, byte for byte). `None`, or a material top at or under Top Z, gives the new ladder.
- Round 3: `camcraft_motion::approach::Approach` gets the runtime field `material_top: Option<f64>` (default `None`, not in the project file). The callers that carry `links` use `cut_levels_under`: pocket, HSM pocket, trochoidal pocket, adaptive trochoidal, slot, contour, bore, circular (not vault), 3D entry ladder.
- Round 3: `crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs` sets `material_top` from `stock_top_z` (in the generator frame). `crates/app/src/operation/area.rs`: `ladder_planes` reads the same material top (part top or setup stock top), so the region planes are the generator levels.
- Round 3: `crates/motion/src/machining2d/contour_bore.rs`, `contour_step.rs`, `contour.rs`: a bore-side level transition whose column no earlier descent opened starts at the top of the cut plus the plunge height. It does not start at the floor of the level before.
- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/circular.rs`: vault mode. A plane at Top Z is dropped. An inner ring keeps the floor of the ring before it as its first level.
- `crates/motion/src/turning/face.rs`: a rung exactly at the top of the work is dropped.
- Decisions: `docs/decisions/2004-top-z-level.md` (items 3 and 4d are now decided).

Posted G-code changes: each depth-stepping operation that uses the level law cuts one level fewer (the air level at Top Z), unless stock stands over Top Z. Then the program keeps the old levels. The bore-side helix transition of the first level now starts 2 mm (plunge height) over the top of the cut. This is under the safety floor.


## Round 5 (head `b18b928131467a963022f3efcd6bc6352fd07599`)

Code:
- `TraceParams` and `TrochoidParams` get `material_top: Option<f64>`. `trace` and the trochoidal slot `finish` use `cut_levels_under`. `generate.rs` fills the field for Trace, Engrave and Trochoidal slot from `lk.approach.material_top` (the stock top). `trochoid_op::trochoid_params` takes it as a parameter. The lanes of 2D Adaptive (Trochoidal) copy it from the pocket links. Decision item 9.
- With Top Z under the stock top, no first cut of these operations is deeper than one stepdown.

Recorded files changed (the only change is the loss of the air level at Top Z):
- `crates/post/tests/recorded/inputs/vertical_arc_x.cl`: 33 to 22 moves. The Z 0 level is gone. The Z -2 entry arc is the same circle (centre X17 Z6), entered from the plunge height Z 2 over Top Z.
- `crates/post/tests/recorded/inputs/vertical_arc_y.cl`: 33 to 22 moves. The same change in G19 (centre Y7 Z6).
- `crates/post/tests/recorded/inputs/vertical_arc_oblique.cl`: 54 to 40 moves. The Z 0 level is gone. The chord descent of the first level starts at Z 2 over Top Z.
- Posted output change (post `vertical_arc_entry`): one G18 or G19 arc block fewer, two instead of three (levels Z -2 and Z -4). The test now counts 2. The plane words and the Heidenhain law are not changed.

Tests (debug), round 5:
- New: `top_z_level::a_trace_under_stock_over_top_z_keeps_the_level_at_top_z`, `top_z_level::a_trochoidal_slot_under_stock_over_top_z_keeps_the_level_at_top_z` (motion); `top_z_stock_over::a_trace_under_stock_over_top_z_keeps_the_level_at_top_z`, `top_z_stock_over::a_trochoidal_slot_under_stock_over_top_z_keeps_the_level_at_top_z` (app, levels `[18, 15, 12]` on a stock top of 20).
- Green: motion `top_z_level` 13, `trochoid_slot` 11, `machining2d` 66, `vertical_arc_entry` 3 (after `WRITE_GOLDEN=1`); post `vertical_arc_entry` 3.

- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

Goldens, run without regeneration (red, not changed):
- `golden_cl` 12 of 33 red: `face_square_40x40_stepped` (levels 4 to 3), `contour_plate_with_hole`, `contour_plate_with_hole_blended`, `contour_disc_hole`, `contour_tangential_lead`, `pocket_waterline`, `pocket_zigzag_plate_with_island`, `pocket_zigzag_plate_with_island_blended`, `slot_fullwidth_centerline`, `slot_wide_channel_rows`, `trace_plate_with_hole`, `circular_ring_arcs`. - `solid_law_goldens` 4 of 7 red: `every_depth_law_golden_verifies_exactly_as_before` and `every_posted_golden_is_a_program_the_gate_passes` (stale golden: `contour_disc_hole.cl` 69 to 46 moves, the Z 0 level is gone); `the_slot_trace_and_plasma_goldens_pass_their_gates` (`slot_fullwidth_centerline.cl` 14 to 9 moves, the Z 0 level is gone); `a_lead_on_the_rings_own_circle_is_refused` (the crossing list loses the two crossings of the third level, 6 to 4; the refusal stays).

## Round 4 (head `44ebc51dd1e6d5807af4f49237c66f49ce284f6e`)

In the window v 0 to 8 the bar has rho 2.0 or less. The old levels were `[2.5, 1.5, 0.5]`, and only the level 2.5 had open area, with the tip on the stock skin. That program cut only air. The window v 19 to 28 is the same case. The test now pins the two windows as refusals by name ("nothing to cut"). The station asserts use windows with material: v 0 to 12 (cuts at z 12 or less) and v 10 to 28 (cuts at z 10 or more, more than 20 cuts). Decision item 8.

Code defects found in round 4: none. No gouge, verify, load or solid check is loosened.

Fixtures changed in round 4 (each old expectation counted the Top Z air level):
- `rotary_adaptive::a_window_too_narrow_for_the_helix_is_refused_by_name_before_planning`: the r7 skin level 7.0 was air. The refusal tag is now `ring_tag(5.0)`. An added assert: the r7 skin has no level.

- `entry_arc::the_bore_contour_enters_each_level_on_a_tangent_arc` 3 to 2 fans; `the_wall_side_enters_on_a_tangent_arc_in_the_air_beside_the_wall` 3 to 2.
- `face_blend::conventional_and_staged_blend_every_level`: 12 to 8 arcs (levels -0.5, -2.0).
- `face_holes::staged_facing_lifts_over_the_hole_at_every_level`: plunges 3x to 2x. An added assert: no feed at z 0.
- `machining2d`: face steps `[4,3,2]` to `[3,2]`; face level snap `[4.5,3,2]` to `[3,2]` and `[4.5,2.5,2]` to `[2.5,2]`; contour level snap 4 to 3 plunges; tabs 6 to 5; `levels_3_zs()` is now `[-3, -6]`; zigzag fills 3 to 2, hops 12 to 8; waterline island bottom -3 to -6 (keeps two levels); zigzag clearance lifts 3 to 2; slot fill 3 to 2; trace loops 6 to 4; ramp, entry family and roughing rings start at -3.
- `circular_arcs`: 52 to 48 arcs (12 levels), ramps 26 to 24 or more.
- `arcs`: plain arcs 8 to 4, led 12 to 6, halves 2 to 1, closing 2 to 1.
- `corner_blend`: l_boss 3 to 2; bore 9 to 6 (notes "6 of 8 walked corner(s) rounded", "2 of 8 ... kept sharp"); plate hole 9 to 6; three z loops `[0,-2,-4]` to `[-2,-4]`.

title: feat(gate): one step for each test binary in quick, batch and release
body:
Process change: yes

What changed
- `cargo xtask gate quick`, `batch` and `release` plan one step for each test target of the debug suites, as the heavy lanes do (#1714). Step names: `<crate> suites: lib`, `bins`, `<binary>`, `doc`.
- Batch and release start with one build step (`cargo test --no-run`). Quick builds one time for each crate when the crate has more than one run step.
- Each step has its own log, time and pass or fail line. `--only "app suites: cmds"`, `--failed` and `--dry-run` work for one step.
- Batch keeps `lib` and the binaries, without `SLOW_BINARIES` (as before). Release adds `bins` and `doc`. The ui steps keep CWD `crates/ui`.
- The gate skill, the AGENTS.md tier table and the xtask usage text describe the new steps.
- Decision: `docs/decisions/1941-gate-step-per-binary.md` (steps run in the same order as before; release keeps its waves; a step runs `cargo test -p x --test b`, no direct exe).

Plan sizes (`--dry-run`, this tree)
| Tier | Steps before | Steps after |
|---|---|---|
| batch | 10 | 713 |
| release | 189 | 911 |
| quick (for a diff) | one step for each crate | one step for each target, and a build step |

Measured (Windows, this machine)
- 7 geometry targets, build ready: one grouped cargo call 1.5 s. Seven steps through `cargo xtask gate batch --only "geometry suites"`: 5.0 s. So one cargo start is about 0.5 s. No step rebuilt anything (each ran in 0 s).
- Estimate, not measured: about 6 min more serial time in batch for 713 steps.
- Not measured: a full batch gate before and after (about 20 min each), and any Linux runner time. The release wave parallelism is unchanged.
- Follow-up #1951 (P7): run the exes from the cargo JSON paths to remove the cargo start.

Pinning tests (`cargo test -p xtask`, 141 pass)
- `step_tests::release_runs_every_target_of_every_crate_one_step_each`
- `step_tests::batch_runs_lib_and_each_non_slow_binary_one_step_each`
- `step_tests::only_and_failed_select_one_binary_step`
- Updated: `tests::batch_skips_slow_binaries_and_release_runs_everything` and the quick plan tests.

Test count: no `#[test]` changed in the crates. The step targets of each crate equal the targets of `cargo test -p <crate>` (batch: minus `bins`, `doc` and the slow binaries, as before). The step tests pin this for every crate.

Real runs: `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main` (xtask unit tests, green) and `cargo xtask gate batch --only "geometry suites"` (7 steps, green). Not run: a full batch or release gate; a quick gate over app or ui steps.

Changelog: Gate: quick, batch and release plan one step for each test binary, with its own log and time.

title: feat(contour): Start point and Exit point rows on the Lead tab
body:
## What changed
The closed 2D contour already takes a user-set start point (#1478) and exit point (#1492) through the project file and MCP `edit_operation`. The GUI had no door to them. This PR adds that door, as typed coordinates:

- The 2D Contour "Lead in / Lead out" tab has two new optional groups, "Start point" and "Exit point". Each group is switched on in its header, like Plunge and Engagement.
- Each group has an X row and a Y row in model coordinates ("Start X", "Start Y", "Exit X", "Exit Y").
- One visible line under the rows says the safety rule: a point that the lead cannot fit at is refused by name, and the point never moves.
- Off writes `None`, which is the automatic seam (the same as every earlier file). On seeds the model origin.
- The rows edit the draft params. Apply commits them through `EditOperationParams`, so Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Y restore the earlier point.
- Other kinds draw neither group. They refuse a point by name (`OpParams::named_refusal`), so a row there could only produce a refusal.

New file `crates/ui/src/egui_app/start_exit_rows.rs` (74 lines) and one call in `approach_page.rs`. No change to the generator, a command, the project file or MCP.

## Images
Rendered with the real page code in an `egui_kittest` harness (a 2D Contour with a start point of X12.5 Y-20 in its params). "Before" is this branch with the one new call removed, which is the page code of main.

Lead in / Lead out tab, before: ![](https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/blob/8b952e0f9bdcc7cf4285643e2efad18b14c1a83a/issue-1448/before-lead-tab.png?raw=true)

Lead in / Lead out tab, after: ![](https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/blob/8b952e0f9bdcc7cf4285643e2efad18b14c1a83a/issue-1448/after-lead-tab.png?raw=true)

## Tests
New `crates/ui/src/egui_app/start_exit_tests.rs` (4 tests, structural: AccessKit labels, roles, toggled and enabled state):
- `the_contour_lead_tab_has_both_point_groups_off_by_default`: both groups are on the tab, their header switches are off and enabled, the X/Y rows are not in the tree, and drawing the tab writes no point.
- `a_typed_start_point_applies_through_the_history_and_undoes`: the switch seeds (0, 0) and shows the rows and the consequence line. A typed X of 12.5 edits only the draft. Apply commits (12.5, 0) and leaves the exit unset. Undo gives `None` again, and redo gives (12.5, 0) again.
- `switching_the_exit_point_off_clears_it`: a saved exit shows its group on with its rows; the switch off writes `None` and removes the rows.
- `kinds_without_a_picked_start_draw_neither_group`: 2D Pocket and Face draw neither group.

Updated `every_field_lives_on_exactly_one_section`: "Start point" and "Exit point" are on the Contour's Lead tab only.

Readings:
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main` on 91e51a2db: green. ui lib 820 passed, 6 ignored (snapshot lane); `boundary` 3, `boundary_picks` 6, `sinker_setup` 2, `theme_files` 14 passed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

Output with no point set: unchanged. This PR touches no generator, post or project-file code, so the goldens are the same by construction; the gate selected no app, motion or post suite.

## Project file and MCP
- Project file: no new field (the fields shipped in #1478 and #1492). No version bump.
- MCP: no new command. `edit_operation` already takes `links.approach.start_point` and `exit_point`.

## Not exercised
- The pixel snapshot lane (release only; no PNG changed).
- A generate from the GUI after Apply. The generator law for a picked point is pinned by the motion `contour_start` and app `contour_start_point` suites, which this PR does not touch.
- Inch display: the rows use the shared `num` unit lens, the same as every other length row.

## Left for later
#1473 holds the rest: the viewport pick on the wall (item 2), compensation (4), open chains (5), tilted contours (6) and other operations such as the Pocket entry point (7). Item 3 (tabs) is PR #1822. This PR uses `Refs`, so #1448 stays open.

Decision: `docs/decisions/1448-start-exit-rows.md`.

Changelog: The 2D Contour's Lead in / Lead out tab has Start point and Exit point groups, where you type the X and Y at which the cut starts and leaves the closed contour.

title: feat(wire-edm): per-ruling kerf widening and a stated verify tolerance for 4-axis cuts
body:
## What changed

A 4-axis Wire Contour had one widening for the whole cut: every ruling stood off the profiles as far as the worst twist needs. The straight stretches of a punch were then oversize. The wire verify also read a tessellated loft's facets as a gouge of a few microns, with no way to state the model's chord tolerance.

- **Motion** (`crates/motion/src/wire_edm/ruled_widen.rs`): `WireWidening { PerRuling, Uniform }`. `PerRuling` is the default. Each ruling stands off by what its own twist needs. Transition rulings 1 mm from the ends of a long span end the widening near the twist. The existing ruled kerf law judges the emitted wire at every height. A path that fails it is refused by name.
- **Sim** (`crates/sim/src/verify/wire/`): `WireJob.verify_tol`. The kerf law lets a reading enter the facets by no more than the stated tolerance. The threading law and the slug law do not use it. A tolerance that is negative, not finite or not below the kerf offset is refused as unreadable. A gouge names the deepest reading at any height.
- **App**: the 4-axis block stores `widening` and `verify_tolerance` (0 to 0.25 mm at the operation door). The two values go through `EditOperationParams` and the project file. The widening is in the stamp digest. The post gate's report line states the tolerance and the deepest reading that it let pass. A 4-axis gouge with no stated tolerance adds a hint that names the model's chord tolerance.
- **UI**: the operation page shows "Stand off" and "Verify tolerance" in the 4-axis block.
- **Docs**: `site/content/guide/operations-edm.md`, `docs/decisions/1170-wire-ruling-kerf.md`.

There is no new command. The MCP surface takes the two keys through the operation parameters DTO (`four_axis.widening`, `four_axis.verify_tolerance`).

## Readings

Motion, square 10 to round 8, 64 points, twist tolerance 0.05 mm:

- Per ruling: the middle of each side stands as a plain taper of its lean (less than 0.003 mm more than the kerf offset). The rulings next to the corners stand 0.015 to 0.05 mm more.
- Uniform: every ruling stands 0.0207 mm more. The note says `the wire is held 0.1857 mm off both profiles`.
- A punch with one twisted flank: `9 of 13 rulings stand within 0.0001 mm of the kerf offset`.

App, square 8 lofted toward a circle, faceted at a chord tolerance of 0.0117 mm:

- No tolerance: `Punch1: wire gouge: the kerf of move 2 enters the part by 0.0004 mm near X-8.019 Y-0.833 at Z2.001 (64 move(s) gouge; the deepest reading at any height is 0.0112 mm) - a tessellated loft's facets stand past its ruled surface by up to the chord tolerance of the model: ...`
- Tolerance 0.0028: refused, `..., past the stated verify tolerance 0.0028 mm (40 move(s) gouge; the deepest reading at any height is 0.0112 mm)`.
- Tolerance 0.0117: posts. The report line says `kerf judged under the stated verify tolerance 0.0117 mm: the kerf enters the model's facets by at most 0.0112 mm, near X-7.468 Y-7.980 at Z6.000`.
- Tolerance 0.2: refused, `the verify tolerance 0.2 mm is not zero or a positive number below the kerf offset 0.1650 mm`.

## Pinning tests

- `camcraft-motion` lib, `wire_edm::ruled_widen_tests`: `a_square_to_round_punch_is_widened_only_where_it_twists`, `only_the_twisted_flank_of_a_punch_is_widened`, `a_twisted_flank_ends_its_widening_at_the_transition_rulings`.
- `camcraft-sim` lib, `verify::wire::tol_tests` (5 tests).
- `camcraft-app` `wire_verify_tol`: `a_tessellated_loft_posts_under_its_chord_tolerance_and_is_refused_below_it`, `the_widening_and_the_tolerance_are_stored_and_bounded_at_the_door`.
- `camcraft-ui` lib: `wire_four_axis_states_the_stand_off_choice_and_the_verify_tolerance`.

Quick gate on the final head `fc6848cf0`, all green. Rerun on the final head: `camcraft-motion` lib `wire_edm` (33 passed), `camcraft-motion` test `wire_fans` (7 passed), `camcraft-ui` lib `wire` (15 passed, includes the pinning test). `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` are clean. Results after the merge of main, from the worker: `camcraft-app` binaries `wire_verify_tol` (2), `wire_4axis` (8), `solid_law_goldens` (7) passed. Earlier results on the same app code: `camcraft-sim` lib `verify::wire` (20), `wire_fans` (2), `wire_stamp` (7), `golden_cl` (33), `project_roundtrip` (73), `wire_taper_angle`, `wire_contour`, `wire_post`, `wire_tabs`, `wire_burnout`, `wire_readers`, `edm_conditions`, `conformance`, `mcp_wire_contour`, `sodick_wire_post`. The clippy run of `camcraft-sim` and `camcraft-app` was clean earlier and was not run again.

## Screenshots

The operation page, Geometry tab, with the 4-axis block on. The images come from the test harness render. They are on the `screenshots` branch and are not part of this PR.

Before (main): the block ends with "Twist tolerance".

![Before](https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/blob/688073aeff311d345c75a109918bc3279d5cbb0f/pr-1921/before.png?raw=true)

After (this PR): the block adds "Stand off" (default "Only where the surface twists") and "Verify tolerance" (default 0.0 mm).

![After](https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/blob/688073aeff311d345c75a109918bc3279d5cbb0f/pr-1921/after.png?raw=true)
