title: feat(2d): rest machining on the 2D Pocket operation
body:
Fork synced at v0.20.0 (process files at PROCESS_VERSION 71).

## What changed

The 2D Pocket can now cut only what a larger previous tool left. It uses the rest generator of #1446 (`machining2d::rest_pocket`).

- **Parameter.** `OpParams::Pocket` has a new optional `rest` group: previous tool diameter, its corner radius, the stock it left on the walls, and the rest allowance. `None` is off. Off is the default and the plain pocket.
- **Undoable edit.** You change the group through `EditOperationParams`. Undo and redo restore it.
- **Project file.** The key is `rest` (an object). A file without the key reads as off, so the file version does not change.
- **Stamp.** The stamp writes the group (byte `0xD7`) only when it is on. Each value of the group changes the stamp.
- **Generation.** When the group is on, generation calls `rest_pocket`. Its note ("rest machining trusts the entered previous tool ...") goes into the path notes.
- **Refusals by name, in the generator's own words, when you make, edit or retool the operation** (not only at Generate):
  - a previous tool that is not larger than the operation's tool (new `rest_gate`, run from `tool_gate` and from the edit);
  - a value that is negative or not finite, a previous tool diameter that is 0 or less, or a corner radius larger than the previous tool's radius;
  - the Zigzag or Adaptive strategy;
  - pre-drilled entry with rest machining on (`REST_PREDRILLED`). `rest_pocket` does not read the holes, and the program must not drop a user setting without saying so.
- **Motion crate.** `RestParams` has a new `validate_alone` (the checks that do not need a tool, plus "the previous tool diameter must be positive"). The strategy check moved into a public `rest_strategy`. Its text did not change.
- **MCP.** `edit_operation` sets the group (`"rest": null` turns it off). There is a new row in the camcraft-mcp skill. Area: mcp.
- **Not in this PR: the dialog group.** It is not part of "Done means", and it needs before/after screenshots and the UI gate. The page keeps the group as it is when you apply the page. Follow-up: #1815.

## How tested

The new pinning tests are in `crates/app/tests/rest_pocket.rs`:
- `the_rest_pass_cuts_only_the_corners_posts_and_matches_its_golden`: the fixture is a 60 x 40 pocket with 3 mm corners. A 12 mm end mill roughs it, then a 4 mm end mill does the rest pass. The golden is `pocket_rest_corners.cl`. All cuts stay in the corners. The program posts and the verification report is clean.
- `read_against_the_simulated_roughing_pass`: the roughing pass is simulated first on the stock dexel grid. Then:
  - no rapid of the rest pass hits stock;
  - every plunge goes down on floor that is already clear, and its rim touches stock for no more than one level;
  - all 8 rings (4 corners x 2 levels) cut stock, and air is less than half of each ring.
- `the_group_is_an_undoable_edit_and_the_project_file_keeps_it`
- `a_previous_tool_that_is_not_larger_is_refused_by_name_at_the_edit_and_the_retool` (edit, create and retool)
- `values_and_strategies_the_rest_pass_cannot_run_are_refused_by_name`
- `mcp_sets_refuses_undoes_and_saves_the_group` (set, refuse, save, reopen, null, undo)

Other tests:
- `operation::rest_op_tests::the_rest_group_moves_the_stamp`
- `crates/motion/tests/rest2d.rs`: a new case for a 0 mm previous tool.

Mutation check: I deleted each new refusal line, the stamp line and the generation line one at a time, ran the test that pins it, and saw it fail. Then I restored the file and compared it with a backup. All 11 failed when deleted and were restored byte for byte: the motion "must be positive" check, rest_op's three refusals, sane's `named_refusal` and `is_sane` lines, `rest_gate` in `tool_gate`, `rest_gate` in the edit, the refusal arm inside `rest_gate`, the `0xD7` stamp block, and the `rest_pocket` call in generation.

Gate: `cargo xtask gate quick` plans almost the whole workspace for this diff, so I ran the touched suites by name instead (motion: lib, rest2d, machining2d, predrilled_entry, corner_arc_radius, optimal_load, solid_law; app: lib, rest_pocket, golden_cl, arc_turn_params, predrilled_entry, project_roundtrip, roughing2d, adaptive_trochoid, mcp, mcp_pockets, pocket_recognition, operations, commands_undo, tool_gate, tool_law, verify, solid_law_goldens, heights, tilt, corner_blend, climb_direction, area_controls, pick_agnostic, pocket_overhead, units_in_refusals, lead_approach, level_links, whole_model_pocket, recorded_post_streams; ui: lib, edge_loop_pick, operations). All green. Clippy `-D warnings` on camcraft-motion, camcraft-app and camcraft-ui (all targets): clean.

The existing pocket goldens do not change (`golden_cl`, `adaptive_trochoid`, `roughing2d` and the others in the list above).

## What I did not test

- I did not run the program on a machine, and I did not take screenshots (there is no UI change).
- Two things I measured but did not fix, because they are generator behaviour and not part of this slice:
  - The inner leg of each corner ring crosses floor that the 12 mm tool already cleared: 6.7 mm of a 14.8-15.3 mm ring. Follow-up: #1816.
  - On each level, 2 of the 4 corner plunges touch rest material at the rim. The tool axis is over cleared floor. Entry from cleared space belongs to #1490.
- All of these are feed moves, so they cost time, not safety.

Decision record: `docs/decisions/1489-rest-pocket-param.md`.

Changelog: 2D Pocket rest machining: cut only what a larger previous tool left (previous tool entered by hand); undoable, saved in the project, set through MCP; a previous tool that is not larger is refused by name (#1489)

Effort: high (no escalation)

Fixes #1489

title: fix(post): Tormach lathe G76 J makes LinuxCNC's R1 ladder cut the record's passes
body:
## What changed

`assets/posts/tormach-lathe.cps`, `g76Grid`: J (first depth) is no longer floored to the grid on its own. LinuxCNC's G76 with `R1` cuts J, 2J, ... with the last pass clamped at K, so the control cuts ceil(K/J) passes. The record lays n = ceil(height / first depth) equal rungs (g76Why already holds the equal ladder), so J must satisfy (n-1)J < K <= nJ:

- J is the shallower grid rounding (as before) when that keeps the count;
- when the shallower J would add a pass, J is the one grid step up, and never a full grid step over the record's first cut;
- otherwise the record is refused by name: `G76 threading cycle refused - no first depth J on the control's grid makes R1's equal ladder cut the record's n passes (K ...)`.

The root keeps its outward rounding. Peak, root, I and K are unchanged.

## Golden change, line by line

`crates/app/tests/golden/nc/tormach-lathe/thread_g76_inch.nc`, one line:

```
-G76 P0.07874 Z0.315 I-0.004 J0.0314 K0.0944 R1 Q0 H0
+G76 P0.07874 Z0.315 I-0.004 J0.0315 K0.0944 R1 Q0 H0
```

What this relies on, from the public LinuxCNC G-code reference (G76): J is the first cut depth, K the full thread depth (diameters here, under G7), and `R1.0` selects constant depth, so each pass goes J deeper than the last and the last pass is clamped at K.
- Old: 0.0314, 0.0628, 0.0942, then 0.0944 (a 0.0002 in pass) = 4 passes. The record laid and the verdict judged 3 (0.4 / 0.8 / 1.2 mm radius).
- New: 0.0315, 0.0630, 0.0944 (clamped) = 3 passes, the record's count. J 0.0315 in is 0.000004 in (0.1 um) over the record's Ø0.8 mm first cut. The root (X + I - K) is the same as before: never deeper than the minor.
- P, Z, I, K, R, Q, H and every other line are unchanged. The mm golden (`J0.8 K2.4`) is byte-identical.

The earlier PathPilot Hub 8L sim run of this golden (PR #517 comments) does not cover the new J: **this golden needs a new Hub run** (not done here, no Hub access).

Scan (local script, not committed): realistic records (first depth 0.05-0.5 mm, height 0.3-2 mm, four minor diameters, the stream's lattice) - the old rule mis-stated 2.7% of inch records; the new rule miscounts none and refuses none in either unit. Refusals are reached only by records with many tiny rungs (e.g. 0.15 deep in rungs of 0.012, inch) or a lattice disagreement on the crest.

## How tested

New suite `crates/app/tests/lathe_post_tormach_g76_ladder.rs`:
- `g76_words_cut_exactly_the_records_passes_in_mm_and_inch` - parses the posted J/K as grid steps, counts ceil(K/J) and asserts it equals both the G33 pass count of the same document and ceil(height / first depth) of its record; asserts J is under one grid step over the record's first cut.
- `g76_refuses_by_name_when_no_grid_j_cuts_the_records_passes` - mm: crest +2 um (inside the lattice allowance) makes K 2.402, refused (J 0.801 would be a full step heavy); inch: 0.15 deep in 0.012 rungs, K 118 steps, no whole J with 12J < 118 <= 13J, refused.

Updated: `a_thread_posts_as_one_g76_block_with_the_option_in_mm_and_inch` (inch line J0.0315, golden regenerated).

Mutation checks (each mutation applied, suites run, file restored and touched):
- delete `if (j < lo) j = lo;` -> both new tests red (and the golden test);
- delete the refusal `return { why: ... }` line -> refusal test red;
- drop the `j <= hi` half of the refusal condition -> refusal test red (inch case);
- drop the `j - jRec < 1` half -> refusal test red (mm case).

`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: green (post suites 5 s, app suites 1648 s - the shared golden pulled every app suite). `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --test lathe_post_tormach_g76_ladder --test lathe_post_tormach_thread -- -D warnings`: clean.

Not exercised: a PathPilot / LinuxCNC run of the new inch golden; no batch gate (budget).

## Overlaps

- #517 and #518 (G76 on both lathe posts): `git merge-tree` with each branch is clean (#517 changes `g76Why`, this changes `g76Grid`), so not stacked. With #517's finish-allowance rule the record's rung count is still ceil(height / first depth).
- #1667 and #1681 conflict with this on adjacent lines of the same inch golden and `lathe_post_tormach_thread.rs` (their G30 / drive-line changes next to the G76 line): a mechanical keep-both, regenerate the golden at merge.

Decision record: `docs/decisions/1619-g76-inch-ladder.md`.

Fork synced at v0.19.0 (branched from upstream/main 058e14ca).

Changelog: Tormach lathe G76 (inch) states a first depth J whose LinuxCNC R1 ladder cuts exactly the verified passes (J0.0315, not 0.0314, on the M12x2 fixture); a record no grid J can state is refused by name.

Effort: high (no escalation)

Fixes #1619

title: fix(ui): keep the near plane and the ortho eye consistent with the zoom
body:
### Summary

A viewport fix for the way the camera eats the model from the inside.

Two ways the camera clipped the model while zooming:

- **Perspective:** the near plane was a fixed 0.1 mm from the eye, so at close zoom the geometry right in front of the near plane clipped instead of rendering — zooming in went through the model. The near plane now rides `dist` (0.1 % of the view depth, clamped to 1e-5 min and 0.1 max).
- **Orthographic:** `dist` moved the eye, so zooming dollied the eye into the model and clipped through its faces from inside. The eye now sits at a fixed nominal distance (100 mm) behind the target, and `dist` is only a zoom factor for the view box's half-height — the way it was always meant to work. The near plane now reaches far behind the eye plane: `-((dist * 20.0).max(1000.0) - ORTHO_EYE_DIST)`.

Changelog: UI — the perspective near plane moves with the dolly distance and the orthographic camera's near plane no longer clips through geometry while zooming.

The tests pin the new ortho depth formula and a point in front of the eye plane (`dist = 300`, 150 mm back from the target), asserting it stays inside the clip volume.

### Verification

`cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib` — 803 passed. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui --all-targets` — clean. No posted G-code, collision check, stock simulation math or geometry changed.

No issue covers this viewport bug yet — a maintainer will file one.

## The citation gate (the issue's precondition)
Before any code, the issue required a primary-source citation that chained Fanuc G32 blocks keep spindle synchronization. Found in *FANUC Series 0i-TD/0i Mate-TD USER'S MANUAL (For Lathe System)*, B-64304EN-1/01, Part II:
- **§3.4 "Continuous Threading", p.34:** consecutive threading blocks keep "the synchronism with the spindle" at "the joint between blocks wherever possible", so the lead and shape can change midway.
- **§3.2 "Constant Lead Threading (G32)", WARNING 6, p.32:** a threading block that follows a threading block starts "without waiting for detection of the one-spindle-rotation signal".
- **§3.2, pp.29-31:** G32 cuts tapers (`G32 X41.0 Z29.0 F3.5`). Up to 45° the lead F is taken along Z.

The manual was read from a public third-party mirror of Fanuc's PDF (https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/fanuc-0itd-users-manualpdf/259106078), for behaviour only. The Haas G32 reference (cited in #363) agrees. **LinuxCNC G33 stays unconfirmed:** its docs don't say whether a chained G33 waits for the index again, so no LinuxCNC post may declare the capability.

## What changed
- **Parameters.** The infeed plan gains `ThreadInfeed.dips` with interval, height and length. An interval of 0 means off, which is the default.
- **Shape of a dip.** A dip is a radial lift on **roughing passes only**. Each ramp stays under 45°, keeping the lead on Z.
  - **Never placed in:** the first or last lead, or the finishing, spring or #418 repeat passes.
  - **Height:** no more than every dipped pass's depth of cut.
- **New CL segment.** A dip is a variable-radius XY half-turn: the axial travel is still exactly half a lead, but the end radius differs from the start.
- **Marking.** The thread record carries `chip_break_dips`: `DIP 1` in the stream, `ChipBreakDips` as a post property, and a project cache key only when set. The section carries `PARAM ChipBreakDips`. If dips are on but the record can't be attached, the kernel refuses, so a dip is never laid unmarked.
- **Post capability flag.** The engine refuses dips by name for any script without `continuousThreading = true`. Only `fanuc-lathe.cps` declares it, with the citation in its header.
  - It writes each dip segment as `G32 X Z F`.
  - It refuses by name a segment that doesn't continue a G32 chain, is steeper than 45°, or goes deeper than its plunge.
  - **G76 refuses dips by name.**
- **Verdict.** `thread_warnings` checks every chain for phase (equal axial advance per half-turn), depth, slope and placement. Any breach is a Gouge, which blocks the post.
- **UI.** Three rows on the Passes tab.
- **Defaults are byte-identical.** With dips off there is no stamp byte, project key, stream word or PARAM.
- `docs/decisions/419-thread-dips.md`
